note: Resistance budget for the four published acceptance points, before and after moving the package spreader out of the 3D-ICE stack and into the boundary. Analytic budgets only -- no 3D-ICE solve yet, so this establishes FEASIBILITY, not that the gate passes. 25 Aug 2026.
why: As stack layers the lid and cold plate are columns exactly the width of the die, so the package budget scales as 1/area. On the 71 mm^2 Ryzen that gave 0.4675 K/W against a published junction-to-ambient of 0.3962 -- the package alone exceeded the entire budget, leaving a negative share for the cooler. That is not a tuning error, it is impossible, and it is why two of four points could not be reached at any flow.
method: Lee/Song/Moran/Yovanovich constriction correlation, cooling_spec.spreading_resistance_K_per_W, wrapped by sink_models.SpreadingSink. The stack keeps only genuinely die-sized layers (die attach); the lid becomes the spreading base and grease and cold plate act over the base area.
spreading_base: Sized as a fixed LID footprint (~1825 mm^2), not by cooler class. The cooler class sizes the FINS, which is right for convection and wrong for spreading: a 3 mm copper lid cannot spread to the 118 mm extent of a tower cooler. Using the fin extent demanded a 0.0028 K/W cooler for the Ryzen point, which is not a thing that exists.
open: Ryzen still requires ~0.046 K/W of external cooling against a typical tower's 0.10-0.15. The suspected cause is that the cold plate is modelled as a series slab at LID area rather than as a second spreading stage at its own larger footprint; a two-stage die -> lid -> cold plate model should relax it. The correlation is also ~18% conservative in its worst corner. Neither is resolved here.
status: feasibility established; the gate itself has not been re-run
